The rules PvNavBar enforces

The app had three bottom bars and each had been fixed once, by a different pass, so each had a different half of the same fix. A component on every screen of every stage cannot be three components. They now delegate to one, and differ only in their tabs and their accent.

Nothing moves when you switch tabs. Every tab is icon-above-label, always, active or not. Two of the three bars used to turn the active tab into a horizontal pill, so selecting a tab re-flowed the row and the other four labels slid sideways. The transition is now a colour crossfade and nothing else — there is no geometry left to animate.
No container behind the active tab. Not because Material 3’s pill is bad design, but for two reasons of our own: our labels are always visible, so the label already says which tab she is on and colour says it again — a container is a redundant third signal. And action is the only saturated colour this app spends; a filled violet shape parked on every screen at all times spends that meaning down to nothing.
The inactive label must be readable. It was neutral400 — 2.73:1 against the app ground, when WCAG AA asks 4.5:1. The most-seen text in the entire app was at well under half the required contrast. It is neutral600 now: 5.28:1.
Two changes mark the active tab — colour and weight. Never one alone.
Labels never hide, never wrap, never go below 11px. And every tab is Expanded, so the row shares its width evenly and cannot overflow however large the user’s text scale is. A five-tab bar that overflows at 1.3× is a crash for exactly the person who set it.
The bar floats on a tinted shadow. Distinct from the page without a hard border.

How a tap moves you
An IndexedStack. All five pages are built once and stay alive; a tap changes AppNav.instance.index and nothing is pushed or popped. So scroll position, form state and controllers survive tab switches, the hardware back button does not step between tabs, and there is no "back to Today" — Today is always underneath. A tap also records one UsageEvents.screen(), keyed by position rather than by label so a language switch cannot split one surface into two.
Built in lib/screens/main_scaffold.dart → PvTabBar → PvNavBar

lib/screens/today_home_screen.dart · route — (IndexedStack slot 0)

A wrapper, not a screen. It decides which of three Todays is on screen — Classic (the shipped home, home_screen_b.dart), Focus, or V3 — from a session-only TodayVersionStore that always starts on Classic. The Classic | V3 pill floats top-right on the page itself.

What is on it
Brand header — Mark + wordmark, then three round icons: Saved hub, global search, and the avatar. There is no Profile tab in this design — the avatar is the only way to Profile.
Three stage doorways — Parenting (pushes route pp/my_child), Trying-to-Conceive (pushes ttc/today), and Skilling (preview, UI only). These are how you leave this bottom bar for another one.
Weekly Snapshot — The hero: week, day, a one-line brief for the week, trimester progress, and “View week ›”.
Today’s parenting tip — GrowModule — the featured editorial read of the day.
Today’s Journey — The daily stack: Today’s Video, Daily Garbh Sanskar, My Journal, medication & supplements, Daily Reads, and a product carousel.
Commerce, at the foot — Launch Spotlight and the invite nudge. Both render nothing when nothing is live, which is most mornings.

How a tap moves you
Not an IndexedStack — a pop-then-push. openTtcTab runs popUntil(isFirst || name == "ttc/today") and then pushes the target as a named route. So Today is always at the bottom of the stack, every other tab is one route above it, and hardware-back from any tab returns to Today. Each tab screen is rebuilt on entry — nothing is kept warm.
Built in lib/screens/ttc/ttc_common.dart → TtcBottomNav → PvNavBar, floated by TtcPage

The bar

Trying to Conceive — V3

Anyone whose TtcHomeVersionStore is on V3. This is the design the stage is moving to; V1 is the revert path, not the other arm of a live experiment.

0Today
1Learn
2Products
3Tools
4You
How a tap moves you
Same pop-then-push over ttc/today. Two things are different and both have bitten before:

1. The tab set is chosen by the store, not by the caller. TtcBottomNav.v3 used to be a bool defaulting to false, and only two screens passed it — so every screen reached through TtcPage drew V1’s five tabs under a V3 app. It is nullable now, and null means “ask the store”. A default that is wrong for most callers is not a default, it is a trap.

2. The active index is translated by route name. TtcPage(tab: 3) means Calendar in V1 and “Talk to expert” in V3, so reusing the index would highlight a tab the screen has nothing to do with. ttcV3ActiveFor maps the route; anything unrecognised lands on More, which is the truth rather than a fallback.
Built in same TtcBottomNav, v3 resolved from the store
0TodayTtcHomeV3
lib/screens/ttc/ttc_home_v3.dart · route ttc/today

A photographic hero field the page slides over, then a sheet of sections. The big fact is where she is, never a probability, never a countdown, and never a “chapter N of 5” — chapters 2–4 come round with every cycle.

What is on it
Cycle header — Replaced the chapter hero. Leads on the week and the window, with the chapter as a chip above them. Carries avatar, date strip and a calendar icon.
My daily insights — Titled with the selected date, not the word “Today” — a heading saying “Today” over cards computed for last Tuesday is a screen lying about its own contents.
Start anywhere — The bracket door grid, four columns, one per TTC bracket.
Garbhadhana Samskara — The pre-conception practice — the ritual card in full, with checkboxes and a streak. Not Garbh Sanskar, which is the pregnancy feature and a different thing.
Recommended for you — A product rail. Shows category and price, never a benefit — a supplement rail on a fertility home is one careless subtitle away from being a claim.
Recommended reads — The chapter card, then Me / Us / What’s next tabs hung off it, then a rail into the reads library.
Your journal — Pregnancy’s widget verbatim, with four quick actions.
Talk to experts — The section that ends the page — deliberately not the products rail. The last thing she reads is that there is a person, not a price.
The door out — The positive-test door, plus the disclaimer.

How a tap moves you
⚠️ This is the one bar that is not the pill. It is a hairline-topped white bottomNavigationBar, 62pt, with filled/outlined icon pairs — not PvNavBar, not floating, not rounded. It switches with a plain setState over five bodies, so like pregnancy there is no push and no back between tabs. It is deliberately calm and clinical: a work tool, not the warm parent experience.

The shell also keeps the roster fresh three ways — on app resume, on a 90-second poll (for the phone left open on a desk, which never resumes because it never left), and by pull-to-refresh. Prescriptions ride along, because every screen decides what to say about a past consult from PrescriptionStore.hasFor().

Commentary

What a review should decide on

Everything above is what the app does. This page is judgement — the seven things worth an argument, written so they can be agreed or dismissed rather than rediscovered.

high

The same five words mean two different things

“Prepare” in pregnancy is four category rows: Courses & Cohorts, Birthing Classes, Yoga, Nutrition. “Prepare” in TTC V1 is nine categories of paid offerings. “Tools” in pregnancy is a 20-tile grid sorted by stated priorities; “Tools” in TTC is 22 tiles in four named groups; “Tools” in parenting is seven tracker rows. A woman crossing TTC → pregnancy → parenting meets the same five labels three times and has to relearn what is behind two of them. Worth deciding whether that is intended.

high

Three different navigation mechanics under one visual component

Pregnancy is an IndexedStack (state survives, back does not step between tabs). TTC and parenting are pop-then-push (state is rebuilt every entry, back always returns to tab 0). The doctor app is a setState over five bodies in a completely different bar. The pill looks identical in the first three, so the difference is invisible until something depends on it — a half-typed post, a scroll position, an in-progress log.

medium

Ask Veda has no permanent home on the parenting side

It lost its tab to Brain Development and now lives on the My Child page and the floating FAB. The FAB is present, so nothing is unreachable — but the stage that most invites a question is the one where asking is not on the bar.

high

Every V3 nav change costs an entrance somewhere

V3 dropped Calendar and Community and split Prepare; TtcMoreScreen is the entire compensation, and seven Prepare categories hang off one row in it. The parity test covers the two homes, not the bars. If a tab is ever added to V3, whatever it displaces needs an entrance before the change lands — that is the direction that breaks.

medium

Eight version toggles, four of them reachable from a bottom tab

Today (Classic|Focus|V3), PP Home (Current|V3), TTC Home (V1|V3), Grow (V1|V2|V3) — plus Health Wallet, Scans Hub, Shravan and Baby Naming deeper in. Each is a design question deferred to a runtime switch, and none of them is actually answered: the user still gets whichever we defaulted to. See docs/FLOW-INVENTORY.md.

low

Testing chrome is still on the bar’s doorstep

The Mom | Dad pill floats bottom-right on pregnancy Today (Classic only), the Classic | V3 pill floats top-right, and the doctor-mode toggle sits in the community utility row. All three ship in release builds today. They are listed here so the pre-launch sweep has a list.

low

Nothing floats at a hardcoded offset any more — check new work against that

Every floating control used to sit at bottom: 96, which cleared the bar on a gesture-nav phone and was swallowed by it on a three-button one. pvNavClearance() is the answer, and it reads viewPadding rather than padding because an ancestor SafeArea collapses the latter to zero. Anything new in the bottom strip should use it. (The Mom|Dad pill is a deliberate exception — it was never the control that got swallowed.)
